result.title: On the Informativeness of Structural Stability Bounds for GNNs: GINs versus GATs
result.comment: Extended version of a paper submitted to ESANN 2027
result.summary: Stability bounds for graph neural networks limit how much node representations can drift when the graph changes, but they are rarely compared with the simplest alternative: a bound on the distance between any two outputs, whatever the graph. We derive structural stability bounds for Graph Isomorphism Networks (GINs) and single-head GATv1 networks under deterministic edge perturbations that need not be small, and compare each with such a perturbation-independent diameter bound. For GINs, we characterize exactly when the stability bound is tighter, through a condition linking perturbation size, depth and maximum degree; it holds with a wide margin on Cora, but fails beyond a few layers on the low-degree MUTAG graphs. For GATv1, the bound is never tighter, which calls for analyses based on attention masses.

AI.brief_summary: 论文推导 GIN 与单头 GATv1 在确定性边扰动下的结构稳定性界，并与与扰动无关的输出直径界比较，刻画出何种深度、扰动幅度和最大度条件下稳定性界更紧。
